Definition: Assuming that what is true of the whole must be true of each part. It is the reverse of composition, dividing a group quality down to every member.
Example: A famous university is assumed to mean every single student there must be brilliant in every subject.
FaithDiscussionExample: Someone says, 'The early church was generous, so every individual early Christian must have been generous in every way,' flattening a general description into a claim about each person.
HowToRespond: Keep the whole and the parts distinct: 'A true description of the group does not always describe each member — could we look at the individuals on their own evidence?'
